Such networks often lose accuracy when edges are noisy or when linked nodes tend to differ, a setting called non-homophily. The paper introduces AdvSynGNN, a design that pairs multi-resolution structural synthesis with contrastive goals to build geometry-aware starting representations.

A transformer backbone adjusts its attention with learned topological signals to handle heterophily. An adversarial engine tests possible edge changes against a checker that enforces global coherence. Label fixes then use a residual correction guided by per-node confidence, keeping iteration stable. Tests across varied graph types showed better accuracy at fair cost, and the paper closes with deployment guidance for large-scale use.
arxiv-2602-17371:
David A. Simon led a five-author team testing which neural network designs best model galaxy dynamics. Integral field data has changed galaxy evolution studies. Dynamical models extract crucial insights from motion data, yet most such models assume geometry, velocity ellipsoid shape, and stellar distribution forms that real galaxies violate. Machine learning grows ever more powerful in astronomy, so learning which designs fit dynamical models is an important first step.

The team builds a training set of dynamical models of early-type galaxies using Jeans Anisotropic Modelling, then trains a neural network on that data with JAM parameters and mock photometry as inputs. Relatively simple machine learning designs accurately model JAM galaxies, yielding a big speed increase over traditional JAM modeling. The work maps the design landscape for machine-learning-driven dynamical models.
arxiv-2602-17571:
Sreemanti Chakraborti wrote lecture notes for students who want to hunt ultralight axion-like particles with precision and quantum tools. These light particles are a leading dark matter candidate. In the ultralight range, they would act like a field that swings back and forth in step, leaving time-varying marks on lab gear.

The notes first lay out how such particles couple to plain matter, and why distinct couplings give distinct signals. They then survey two search styles. Conversion searches use haloscopes and helioscopes. Precision tests use clocks, optical cavities, interferometers and solid-state resonators. Each tool's reach, noise and mass range get plain treatment, so readers see how varied tools join up.
arxiv-2602-17671:
Abdulhadi Shoufan and Ahmad-Azmi-Abdelhamid Esmaeil ask how students themselves experience AI hallucination. As students lean more on large language models, false outputs threaten learning, and AI literacy must grow beyond prompt tricks to cover detection and response. The study poses three open questions on experience, detection and mental models.

Sixty-three university students replied. Thematic analysis finds reported troubles center on fake citations, false facts, overconfident but misleading answers, poor prompt adherence, stubborn wrong answers and sycophancy. Students detect flaws by gut judgment or by active checks such as cross-checking sources and re-prompting. Many picture AI as a research engine that invents facts when its database lacks an answer, a misconception the authors say curricula must correct.
arxiv-2602-17871:
Dhruba Ghosh and team test the fine-grained knowledge of vision-language models, a weak spot behind strong benchmark scores. Vision-language models have advanced across visual question answering, visual reasoning, document understanding and multimodal dialogue, built on varied base models, alignment designs and training data. Yet recent work shows they trail on traditional image classification benchmarks that test fine-grained visual knowledge.

The team tests many recent models on fine-grained classification benchmarks and hunts for factors behind the gap between fine-grained knowledge and other vision scores. Ablation tests show a better language model lifts all benchmark scores equally, while a better vision encoder lifts fine-grained classification most. The pretraining stage also proves vital, above all when language model weights stay unfrozen during pretraining. Those insights point toward stronger fine-grained visual understanding and vision-centric skills.
arxiv-2602-18271:
Seohwa Hwang and five co-authors improve multi-test statistics by letting a helper variable set the stage. Their 2026 paper tackles many simultaneous tests on a main variable, where helper variables can precondition whether a main result counts, sharpening power. Two routes are offered, depending on the helper's role.

One route stops testing the main variable when the helper fails a preset condition; the other adjusts the main evaluation criteria by the helper. A copula method links the two variables by building their joint distribution from separate marginals. Numerical studies show the methods hold false-discovery control while beating main-variable-only approaches on power. Applied to Set4Delta mutant data, they select more genes and clarify where they differ from standard practice.
arxiv-2602-18371:
Kévin Le Balc'h and one co-author prove observability inequalities for the Schrödinger equation in Euclidean space. Their 2026 paper treats sets that are thick when measured against decaying densities, a refined notion of covering space that weakens as density fades. Observability here means the whole solution can be bounded by what is seen on such a set.

The proof leans on quantitative uncertainty principles tuned to decaying densities, notably results of Shubin, Vakilian, Wolff, and Kovrijkine. Uncertainty principles limit how sharply a function and its frequency content can both concentrate, and the adapted versions carry that limit into the decaying-density setting. The result extends observability theory to sparser, fading observation geometries.
arxiv-2602-18871:
Diophantine equations ask for whole-number solutions, and the modular method is a powerful tool for ruling them out. Begum Gulsah Cakti, with three co-authors, studies equations of signature (p, p, 2) over number fields in 2026, using that method.

For general number fields satisfying an S-unit condition, an asymptotic result is proved, assuming standard conjectures for fields that are not totally real. That condition is shown for endless families of real quadratic fields. Outside that asymptotic setting, effective results follow. For specific imaginary and real quadratic fields, explicit bounds are found. Beyond those bounds, solutions of the given type cannot occur. The work blends asymptotic theory with concrete, checkable bounds.
arxiv-2602-19271:
Second-order optimizers speed up large-scale training by using curvature, the shape of the loss surface, not just its slope. In federated learning, where clients train locally and a server averages their work, naive versions often wobble or diverge when client data differ sharply. Junkang Liu and five colleagues trace much of that instability to a geometric cause they call preconditioner drift.

Each client builds its own curvature-based coordinate system, so server averaging mixes updates measured in incompatible geometries and corrupts the global direction. Their framework, FedPAC, aligns and corrects those preconditioners before averaging, restoring a coherent descent direction. The paper thus turns a puzzling federated failure into a fixable mismatch, opening second-order methods to settings where data are far from identical.
arxiv-2602-19371:
High-entropy alloys mix five or more metals into one crystal structure, and their superconductivity is still being mapped. Issei Kubo and six co-authors study eutectic Hf-Nb-Sc-Ti-Zr alloys, finding enhanced critical temperature in body-centered cubic phases compared with typical quinary alloys of that structure. Three compositions spanning a broad range of valence electron concentration were examined across annealing temperatures.

Critical temperature rises markedly as annealing climbs from 400 to 600 degrees Celsius, reaching 9.93 kelvin for one composition annealed at 800 degrees. Nearly all samples count as strong-coupling superconductors. One sample annealed at 500 degrees also exceeds the practical critical current density threshold up to about 4 tesla at 4.2 kelvin and 6 tesla at 2 kelvin, attributed to lattice strain and phase instability.
arxiv-2602-19871:
Flames in small combustors burn in distinct regimes: steady flames, flames that repeatedly die and reignite, and flames that propagate. A 2026 arXiv paper by M Ashwin Ganesh and three co-authors studies those regimes in small combustors, combining dynamics analysis with machine learning.

The team stabilizes a premixed methane-air flame inside an optically accessible quartz tube and records light emission, sound pressure, and high-speed images while varying fuel ratio and flow. Recurrence checks and spectral statistics of those signals reveal distinct dynamic signatures for each regime. A stacked ensemble trained on features from both analyses learns to tell the regimes apart. Wavelet plots and phase plots further show how competing timescales interact as regimes evolve.
arxiv-2602-19971:
Relativistic scalar bosons are usually described by the Klein-Gordon equation, which is second order in time. A 2026 arXiv paper by Roland Combescot, working alone, shows they also satisfy a different wave equation, closely analogous to the Dirac equation.

Unlike Klein-Gordon, the new equation is first order in time differentiation, and it reaches the standard Schrödinger equation smoothly in the non-relativistic limit. The wave function in this representation has two components for a scalar boson, mirroring the four components of a spin-half fermion in the Dirac equation. Readers gain a Dirac-like, first-order picture of relativistic scalar particles, with the familiar non-relativistic limit intact.
arxiv-2602-20471:
Tuning optical proximity correction models needs high-quality flat contours from scanning electron microscope images. Da Chen and seven co-authors present SegSEM, a case study in tuning the Segment Anything 2 base model to this task with few labeled cases. The method rests on two rules: data-lean fine-tuning that trains only the model's front ends, and a hybrid design that keeps an older method as a trust-aware fallback.

Tests on just sixty factory images show the approach's promise. The main point is a method recipe for putting base models to work in data-scarce work settings. SegSEM shows that a large general model, well adapted and backed by an older fallback, can serve a niche measurement task without massive labels.
arxiv-2602-20571:
Most benchmarks for automated causal inference grade a system on one number, such as an average treatment effect. Ayush Sawarni and two co-authors argue that this single score mixes two steps: identification, which frames a valid design under stated assumptions, and estimation, which runs that design on finite data. Their benchmark, CausalReasoningBenchmark, holds one hundred seventy-four queries across one hundred thirty-nine real data sets. It draws from seventy-three peer-reviewed papers and three causal-inference textbooks.

Each query asks for an identification spec naming strategy, treatment, outcome, and controls, plus a point estimate with a standard error. Scoring the two parts apart lets the benchmark separate reasoning failures from number errors. Tests with a top language model show it picks the high-level strategy in eighty-one percent, yet full spec correctness falls to thirty-eight percent. The bottleneck lies in design details rather than computation.
arxiv-2602-20771:
Joel Hasbrouck and three co-authors test whether cryptoasset markets price assets in a fair, consistent way. They compare investments that share one main risk factor but differ in a second, smaller risk. That setup yields strict rules any fair market must obey, no matter how traders value either risk.

Their tests strongly reject those rules. Because the rules hold whatever the price of risk, the failure cannot be blamed on risk being mispriced. Instead, the authors read it as proof of market inefficiency, most likely caused by frictions that slow the flow of capital to where it is most needed.
arxiv-2602-20971:
Robust machine learning obeys a law: models must be overparameterized to interpolate robustly, which forces their interpolating functions to be Lipschitz. Mihir More and five co-authors connect that law to robust generalization in this 2026 arXiv paper. Robust generalization asks whether small robust training loss guarantees small robust test loss, a question studied through Rademacher complexity.

The authors show the order of the Lipschitz bound stays the same when the global Rademacher complexity of robust loss classes is used. At local scale, for function subsets with small empirical error, the order shifts with the perturbation radius and a localized concentration term. The work closes an open problem from 2021 by tying the two ideas together for arbitrary data distributions.
arxiv-2602-21071:
Scalar bend stiffness asks when bend bounds force a shape to be a standard form. Dongyeong Ko and Xuan Yao build a new tool for that question in this 2026 arXiv paper: minimal slicing via hair-thin slices, applied to shapes with edges. In 4D, they prove a match-up and stiffness claim for compact shapes with mean convex edges matching a convex Euclidean domain.

Under scalar bend that never dips below zero and a scaled mean-bend match-up along the edge, the shape must be same-shape as the Euclidean domain. A second result handles a hyperbolic twin with fixed bend match-ups, proving the traced form of a Gromov guess on hyperbolic convex domains. Readers get slicing methods that turn edge data into global shape takeaways.
arxiv-2602-21171:
Galaxy disks shine with exp curves, and bouncing may explain why. Curtis Struck, Bruce Elmegreen, and Elena D'Onghia show how in this 2026 arXiv paper. Bouncing of stars by star clouds or massive clumps raises speed spread and pushes the radial curve toward exp form.

Bouncing settles into a steady oval-shape spread, after which oval shapes rise and fall at equal rates: the process rounds out orbits, capping disk heating and keeping motion order. The spread and rounding do not hinge on cloud mass, though heavier clouds reach a rest point faster. A few runs split toward early-type disks, but the main story is a process that builds and keeps exp disks.
arxiv-2602-21271:
Magnetohydrodynamic turbulence has long split experts between two spectral scalings. Manthan Verma, Abhishek Jha, and Mahendra Verma settle the question toward one side in this 2026 arXiv paper, using high-resolution simulations on very large grids. Total energy and cross helicity spectra sit closer to Kolmogorov five-thirds scaling than to the three-halves alternative.

Fluxes and structure functions of total energy and cross helicity robustly support the Kolmogorov picture. Magnetic energy also follows five-thirds scaling, while kinetic energy follows three-halves, a difference traced to energy transfers from magnetic field to velocity field. Readers get simulation evidence that resolves a long-standing controversy, with a mechanism for the remaining split.
arxiv-2602-21371:
Sai Surya Duvvuri and eight co-authors propose Interleaved Head Attention, a fix for a limit of multi-head attention in large language models. Standard attention gives H heads exactly H independent attention matrices. No talk passes between heads while attention is computed. That hurts multi-step reasoning, which must combine evidence from many parts of the context.

Interleaved Head Attention builds P pseudo-heads per head. Each pseudo-head is a learned mix of all H original queries, keys, and values. That creates up to P squared attention patterns per head at modest extra cost. Theory shows fewer parameters on synthetic tasks. Real tests show multi-key retrieval on RULER up 10 to 20 percent. After reasoning fine-tuning, gains reach about 6 percent on GSM8K and about 3 percent on MATH-500.
arxiv-2602-21671:
Lucas Alves Zischler and three co-authors derive secret key rate limits in coexisting classical-quantum optical links. Classical-quantum coexistence enables cost-effective data and quantum transmission over one fiber channel. But weak quantum-key distribution signals suffer nonlinear interference from classical traffic, mainly Raman scattering and four-wave mixing, plus noise.

In quantum-key distribution protocols, higher channel loss and excess noise both cut secret key rates, shown here for BB84 and Gaussian-modulated coherent-states. The study derives closed-form expressions for interference power from classical signals in a quantum frequency channel. The model enables design of classical-quantum systems in single-mode fibers, capturing interference evolution. Applied to frequency allocation in multiband systems, it shows a surprise. Contrary to common practice placing quantum channels in the O-band, higher secret key rates come from the upper E-band and lower S-band across relevant scenarios.
arxiv-2602-21871:
Amar Fakhredine and four co-authors study relativistic spin-momentum locking from altermagnetism under inversion-symmetry breaks, using Ca2RuO4 as test case. The break can yield Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling, Weyl-type coupling, or two lockings. Their work matches the ground state: magnetic order centered on A, Neel vector along b, spin tilts along a and c, no weak ferromagnetism.

Ca2RuO4 shows such locking, with even-parity orders per spin part. Doped samples point from pure altermagnetism to weak ferromagnetism. Ferroelectric-like and antiferroelectric-like distortions leave non-relativistic locking and weak ferromagnetism unchanged, yet Rashba or Weyl coupling grows. Relativistically, other parts take p-wave form under Rashba coupling, while Weyl coupling wrecks nodal planes, leaving only nodal lines. A modulated field shifting atoms in one Ca2RuO4 layer drives an exotic altermagnetic state hosting two non-relativistic lockings with weak ferromagnetism.
arxiv-2602-22171:
Designers now sketch alongside multimodal AI tools, but how creative control actually shifts between person and machine is poorly mapped. Weiyan Shi and Kenny Tsu Wei Choo study sketch-based ideation with an AI-powered system, using interaction logs and post-task interviews from a dozen participants. They sort collaboration into four modes by who holds creative responsibility: human-only, human-led, AI-led, and co-evolution.

Designers rarely stay in one mode; human-led and AI-led roles interweave and shift across ideation moments. The taxonomy gives future work an empirical base for asking why designers switch roles and how tools can better support that dance. For tool builders, the lesson is to design for shifting control, not for a fixed division of labor.
arxiv-2602-22271:
Self-attention is usually described as a flexible way to mix a token with its past. Deepak Agarwal and four co-authors reinterpret causal transformers inside a probabilistic framework. The move mirrors how classical PCA extends to probabilistic PCA. That reformulation exposes a barrier constraint on attention parameters, and a degeneracy boundary where the attention map turns locally ill-conditioned.

The boundary yields a stability-margin reading like the margin in support vector machines, giving rise to support tokens: the tokens that pin down the boundary. The paper also shows causal transformers define a steady random process over endless token sequences, and derives a Bayesian training goal from the view. Robust language modeling gains a new foundation, with margins to measure.
arxiv-2602-22471:
The theta group is a classical object in the theory of modular forms, and its higher-level versions open new ground. Kazuhide Matsuda introduces level three and level four versions of the theta group, extending the familiar structure to finer settings. The paper treats both levels in parallel, building the tools needed to study forms on them.

Matsuda proves that two explicit eta-product functions are modular forms on the level-three and level-four groups respectively. He also computes their multiplier systems, the extra data that pins down how the forms transform. Number theorists gain concrete forms and their transformation data for these higher-level groups.
arxiv-2602-22771:
Yusuke Watanabe and five co-authors ask when a clinical AI should admit it cannot tell. Doctors often decide with incomplete data, and must judge whether the available facts settle the question. Both jumping to conclusions and needless abstention can endanger patients.

ClinDet-Bench turns clinical scoring systems into a test of that judgment, splitting incomplete-information cases into determinable and undeterminable ones. Deciding requires checking every hypothesis about missing facts, unlikely ones included, and seeing whether the conclusion holds across them. Recent models failed the test, judging too soon or abstaining too much, even while explaining scoring knowledge well and succeeding with complete data.
arxiv-2602-22871:
Roy Miles and four co-authors stitch diffusion-model reasoning into stronger answers. Generating many chains of thought helps, but standard aggregation picks whole traces or votes on final answers, discarding useful steps from partial or nearly correct attempts. Stitching Noisy Diffusion Thoughts instead pools step-level candidates.

For each problem, the method samples many cheap, diverse reasoning paths from a masked diffusion language model. It scores every intermediate step with an off-the-shelf process reward model, and stitches the best steps across paths into one composite rationale. Only the final answer is then recomputed. Across math reasoning benchmarks, step-level recombination helps most on hard problems. It lifts average accuracy by up to about twenty-four percent across six math and coding tasks, with latency nearly halved against diffusion and unified rivals.
arxiv-2602-23071:
Yuqi Shi and three co-authors separate fluency from rightness in second-language Mandarin prosody. Learners may master grammar word order yet struggle to map syntax onto fitting prosodic structures. The study probes freezing and steadiness at the syntax-prosody join by weighing 67 Mandarin speakers with 67 Vietnamese learners in the BLCU-SAIT corpus.

By joining C-ToBI break marks with link Grammar analysis, the team tracks break count and links to grammar ties. Results reveal uneven learning: although high-skill learners meet the native norm in break count at Major Phrase level, their frame mapping sharply departs. Namely, high-skill learners downgrade the prosodic break at the Subject-Verb join, while wrongly lifting the Verb-Object break. This tactic allows learners to keep high long phrasal output at the cost of frame rightness. This results in a twisted prosodic ladder where the native pattern is flipped.
arxiv-2602-23471:
Artur Gimranov and six co-authors combine transformers and graph neural networks for sequential recommendation, the task of predicting a user's next item. Transformers capture order in interaction histories but treat items in isolation, while graph networks model links between items but struggle to track how those links change over time.

Their framework aligns both representations: it encodes structural links in the interaction graph and tracks their change over time at once. Tests on a number of open datasets show the combined framework consistently beats pure sequential approaches, pure graph approaches, and recent methods that mix both signals, on recommendation quality. The work thus closes a gap between sequence models and graph models for next-item prediction.
arxiv-2602-23871:
Faisal Hawladera and four co-authors present a cloud-assisted perception system that gives self-driving cars a full 360-degree three-dimensional view while adapting to available bandwidth. The 2026 paper addresses the clash between heavy onboard compute and strict latency limits, which bites hardest in busy urban scenes.

Transformer models fuse multi-camera data into a bird's-eye view for three-dimensional object detection. Work splits between car and cloud, with the split point and feature quantization chosen on the fly; feature clipping and compression cut network load before transmission. Real-world tests show a large latency cut versus a purely onboard system. Under varying bandwidth, the adaptive choice of split and quantization improves accuracy over fixed settings at the same latency, keeping perception timely when networks fluctuate.
arxiv-2603-01771:
Harry Amad and Mihaela van der Schaar predict how a neural network output shifts when its design settings change. Their 2026 work names that task Hyperparameter Trajectory Inference. Settings like reward weights are fixed at design time, yet user tastes can drift after deployment and force costly retraining.

Their approach learns from observed outputs how the output distribution moves as settings vary. A surrogate model then mimics the network at settings never actually trained. The method rests on conditional Lagrangian optimal transport, which learns both the motion law and the best maps between output states. Biases from the manifold hypothesis and least-action ideas keep inferred paths feasible. Tests show the surrogate rebuilds network outputs across setting ranges better than rival methods, which could spare many retrains.
arxiv-2603-01971:
Matheus Barreto, Mario de Castro, Thiago Ramos, and colleagues score how much each single prediction can be trusted. Their 2026 work notes that models can shine on average while a few costly errors dominate deployment bills. Their wrapper, Locus, targets the realized loss of a fixed model, input by input.

Any engine that predicts a distribution for the loss can drive the Locus score. A split-calibration step turns raw output into a distribution-free score with a plain reading. The score reads as an upper loss level and stays comparable across unlike inputs. Rankings alone prove useful, and an optional threshold flags risky cases with controlled large-loss rates. Across thirteen regression benchmarks, Locus ranks risk well and cuts large-loss frequency versus standard heuristics.
arxiv-2603-02171:
Andrew Urilyon, Romain Vasseur, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Jacopo De Nardis model spin transport with rods in this 2026 paper. They extend the hard-rod gas, where particles bounce off each other like stiff rods. Each rod type has its own length, and a clash shifts by the shorter rod's length. The authors argue this setup mirrors a key quantum spin chain.

Matching just how rod speeds fade with length rebuilds the chain's transport map. One regime spreads slowly with odd swings, and the balance point spreads faster. For long rods, path swings look normal in one regime and show a known rough pattern at balance. Charge swings behave in the opposite way at balance. The simple rod picture thus explains strange quantum transport.
arxiv-2603-02271:
Manoj Vishwanathan, Suvinay Subramanian, and Anand Raghunathan profile robot AI models on edge hardware in this 2026 paper. Vision-language-action models let robots link seeing, language, and movement. They must run on local chips, since real-time control cannot wait for the cloud. The team ran a leading seven-billion-parameter model on two chip generations.

One phase dominates the cost: generating the action itself. That phase took up to three quarters of total time and is bound by memory speed. Models and simulations then project what far larger models would need. The authors weigh faster memory and in-memory computing as future fixes. Their map helps chip designers plan for embodied AI at the edge.
arxiv-2603-02471:
Chenyang Zhang, Tianjian Wei, Haoyang Yang, and colleagues rethink web browsing in mixed reality in this 2026 paper. Most XR browsers float a single desktop-style window in space. That habit wastes the room-scale freedom that headsets offer. Their prototype, Break-the-Window, splits a live webpage into spatial panels.

Panels can float mid-air or stick to real surfaces around the user. Touch and ray pointing both move and use the panels. The pages stay fully functional after being split apart. Practitioners first gave formative feedback, then fifteen users explored the prototype. Spatial splitting spread attention and helped users build meaning across panels. Coordination effort, pointing precision, and missing shared conventions caused friction. The authors invite debate on post-window web design.
arxiv-2603-02871:
Clément Argentin, Patrick Chaumet, Michel Gross, and Maxim Yurkin make three rival light-scattering codes agree to the last digit. Their 2026 paper benchmarks the discrete dipole approximation, a method for computing how oddly shaped objects scatter light. Independent codes differ in conventions, settings, and defaults, so fair comparisons were nearly impossible.

Their software-assisted method aligns every free parameter across DDSCAT, ADDA, and IFDDA, reaching machine-precision agreement. Practical equivalence tables let users reproduce each other's runs across codes. They then compare speed on central and graphics processors under several parallel schemes. The package also supports regression testing and exact reproducibility checks for future releases.
arxiv-2603-03171:
Matilde Vicini computes a stubborn two-loop particle process entirely in four spacetime dimensions. The process sends a quark-antiquark pair to a Z boson, with or without an extra photon, while heavy quarks circle a triangular loop. Such axial triangle diagrams are notorious because standard tricks for handling chirality break down when dimensions are stretched.

Her 2026 calculation subtracts infrared, ultraviolet, and threshold singularities all at once, directly in loop momentum space. Anomaly cancellation happens locally in that space, so no dimensional detour is needed. The squared matrix element comes out numerically for both final states. The work serves as a proof that the underlying framework can carry axial couplings in final states, a needed step for precision collider predictions.
arxiv-2603-03271:
Yeasir Rayhan and Walid Aref extend a database buffer trick from two memory tiers to many. Modern machines layer fast local DRAM over slower remote memory and then disk, and database engines must shuffle pages among them constantly. Their 2026 paper generalizes virtual-memory-assisted buffer management to this n-tier world.

The resulting system, vmcache-n, leans on the operating system's virtual memory machinery to migrate pages across tiers. Migration itself can bottleneck, so they add a new system call giving fine-grained control over page movement. On transaction-processing workloads, the design reached up to four times the query throughput of the two-tier predecessor. The work shows operating system cooperation, not just smarter caching rules, unlocks tiered memory for databases.
arxiv-2604-00471: Liu, Lei, and Ren construct and prove unique the Green's matrix for coupled radial Schrödinger equations with symmetric couplings. The matrix is assembled from two families of N independent solutions, regular and outgoing. Its Wronskian matrix turns out diagonal, with entries negative k, and independent of radius. Using the symplectic structure of the doubled phase space, the authors show no other matrix meets the defining equation. It carries the right boundary conditions, continuity at the source, and the prescribed derivative jump.
arxiv-2604-00771: Gjetaj and Weiermann generalize the classical Goodstein process with a new process based on the Hardy hierarchy. They build an ordinal notation system using a two-step collapsing procedure, yielding a proof-theoretic ordinal, and define k-normal forms for natural numbers within it. Their Goodstein-type process cannot be shown to terminate in ID2. ID2 is the theory of non-iterated positive inductive definitions with two operators. That marks a fresh independence finding at the second proof-theoretic threshold.
arxiv-2604-01271: Lebowitz and colleagues use JWST NIRCam imaging from the JEMS survey to map ionized gas in about 200 galaxies at Cosmic Noon. Two tracers, ionized oxygen plus hydrogen-beta and Paschen-beta, are mapped across AGN hosts, Paschen-beta-detected systems, and control objects. Both tracers stretch farther out in AGN hosts than in controls, by about 0.3 dex, with the oxygen-hydrogen tracer modestly more extended than Paschen-beta. The team also measures the radial extent-luminosity relation at redshift near 3 and derives a slope consistent with prior expectations.
arxiv-2604-01571: Du establishes the Affine-Slice Nonvanishing Theorem: a Vandermonde-weighted determinant polynomial is nonzero on non-empty exact-t fibers. The Exact Matching problem asks whether a bipartite graph admits a perfect matching with exactly t red edges. Introduced by Papadimitriou and Yannakakis in 1982, the problem resisted deterministic polynomial-time methods for four decades. This yields a deterministic order-n-to-the-sixth method for Exact Matching via tight-cut decomposition. A Lean 4 formalization accompanies the paper, reducing the theorem to eight hypotheses from results proved here and in McCuaig (2001).
arxiv-2604-01671: Luo and colleagues propose PRCCF, a framework for emotional support chats. Emotional support chats aim to ease distress, but current methods struggle with deep contextual understanding. PRCCF uses persona-guided retrieval jointly matching semantic fit and persona alignment to enhance replies. It uses cause-aware filtering picking cause-linked outside knowledge, lifting contextual understanding for emotional reasoning. Tests on ESConv show PRCCF beats state-of-the-art baselines on machine metrics and human ratings.
arxiv-2604-01771: Recht and colleagues improve large-scale power planning, where linear active-power-only models ignore running constraints. Their approach solves AC expansion problems by re-dispatch and upgrades of an initial plan, adding plants, storage and lines, plus VAR support. It adds startup steps, output curves, and limits on voltage angle gaps and levels. Tested on cases spanning Great Britain and Ireland, with line losses proving most key for the initial plan, while VAR limits add no gain. The result ensures a workable AC system with steady-state voltage stability.
arxiv-2604-01971: Khujakulov and Cocchi compare nonrelativistic and relativistic light absorption by highly charged ions under strong fields. Using the time dependent Schrödinger and Dirac equations with broadband excitation, they model photoabsorption in the dipole approximation. Nonrelativistic scaling with nuclear charge holds exactly in the Schrödinger picture, letting any ion's spectrum follow from a neutral hydrogen like reference. As charge rises, relativistic effects dominate through a strong blue shift from enhanced binding energy, and semi relativistic approximations are judged against Dirac simulations to map where Dirac treatment is needed.
arxiv-2604-02171: Alkan, Grezes, Bartlett, Kelbert, Lockhart and Accomazzi compare two tuning free systems for linking software mentions across documents. Fuzzy matching leans on string similarity, while context aware representations blend mention and document embeddings. Both placed second across all three shared task subtasks with strong F1 scores, context aware winning by a point. Noise tests show complementary weaknesses: context aware resists boundary noise, fuzzy matching handles substitutions better, and context aware scales linearly where fuzzy matching grows superlinearly.
arxiv-2604-02271: Hermann and colleagues measure particle motion from microscopy images with an intensity countoscope. Their real space method tracks intensity fluctuations inside virtual observation boxes of varying size. For small boxes or short times the signal tracks mean square displacement, while for larger boxes and longer times it tracks its square root. A general theory captures both regimes, and a dilute colloidal suspension under confocal microscopy confirms the approach. It extracts diffusion coefficients even where single particles cannot be resolved.
arxiv-2604-02371: Veselka builds a synthetic data pipeline for reasoning in long visual document understanding. The pipeline scores each page for question relevance, extracts textual evidence and orders it from most to least relevant. Supervised fine tuning on the resulting traces, gated by a control token, plus low strength model merging internalizes the reasoning skill. On Qwen3 VL the method scores 58 versus 57 for a far larger sibling model, and on Mistral it beats distillation by about 4 points while using about 12 fewer output tokens.
arxiv-2604-03071: Gloeckle and six colleagues present an automatic AI system formalizing a graduate algebraic combinatorics textbook over 500 pages into Lean. The formalization spans 130K lines and 5900 Lean declarations. Thirty thousand Claude 4.5 Opus agents built it in parallel in one week on a shared codebase through version control. It sets a milestone for textbook formalization scale and a record in multi-agent software engineering. Inference cost matches or undercuts estimated human expert salaries. The Lean codebase and a blueprint website are open-source.
arxiv-2604-03371: Roy and colleagues solve near-best gain choice for two-phase proportional navigation, which steers vehicles to a desired approach angle. Because exact gains for arbitrary geometries are intractable, they train a neural network to map engagement geometries to best gains for each phase. Simulations show the network predicts gains with high accuracy, reaching a fit score close to 0.9.
arxiv-2604-03871: Tianwei Li and team built a fast convexification method for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with polynomial parts. Global optimization of nonlinear models leans on convex relaxations done again and again, whose strength and cost set overall speed and quality. The team used the additive separable shape to reduce relaxation to tight convex envelopes of single-variable polynomials. A continuous Graham Scan variant builds those envelopes exactly via bitangents, yielding bounds often far tighter than leading solvers.
arxiv-2604-03971: Georg Moser and Michael Schaper built Qet, a fully automated static analysis tool for expected costs of mixed classical-quantum programs. Writing quantum programs by hand stays tedious and error-prone, creating demand for tool support. Qet handles mid-circuit measurements and classical control flow, resting on a quantum expectation framework that generalizes Dijkstra's predicate transformer and Hoare logic. Case studies showed Qet inferring precise upper bounds that previously needed tedious manual calculation.
arxiv-2604-04171: David Peter Wallis Freeborn proposed a model of systematic understanding for machine learning systems. On his account, a system counts as understanding a target trait when it holds an adequate internal model that tracks real patterns. That model links to the target through bridge principles and supports reliable prediction. He argued that today's deep learning systems often do achieve such understanding. Yet they fall short of scientific understanding: their grasp is symbolically misaligned, not explicitly reductive, and only weakly unifying, a pattern he called the Fractured Understanding Hypothesis.
arxiv-2604-04271: Panitsas and Tassiulas build TimeRAN, one shared model for the mobile radio access network, replacing many narrow models built per task. The network links phones to towers, and its current AI tools fragment across tasks with poor sharing. TimeRAN learns shared patterns from time series data, then adapts to new tasks with little extra training. It draws on a released corpus of over 355 thousand time series, tops rivals on anomaly detection, forecasting and related tasks, and runs lean in a live 5G testbed.
arxiv-2604-04471: Belousov, Sarkissian and Spiridonov trace how hyperbolic hypergeometric integrals shrink to complex hypergeometric functions. These are Barnes-type products of hyperbolic gamma functions, long known to reduce to plain hypergeometric functions. With even bounds on the integrands, the team shows the one-variable hyperbolic beta and the conical function shrink to flat integrals over the complex plane.
arxiv-2604-04671: Majhi, Mondal and Agnihotri distil four years of research into eight guidelines for game-based refresher training of community health workers in low-resource settings. From quiz apps, real-world, augmented reality, card and location games, they test engagement, learning transfer and local fit. A study among Indian Accredited Social Health Activists and Anganwadi Workers used interviews, field notes and logs. It yields guidelines on realism, adaptive learning, hybrid play, social drive, explainability, work identity and ethics. The result gives researchers and field workers a practical base for poor areas.
arxiv-2604-05171: Li and four colleagues propose NeuroQuant, a 3D coded VAE for brain MRIs. Old VAEs focus on single data, missing other types. It learns a shared latent code across types using focus, catching distant-region links. A 3D encoder then splits body shapes from look. Body codes from a shared book combine with look bits via FiLM in rebuild. On two brain MRI sets it beats old VAEs on rebuild truth, giving model making and cross-modal analysis.
arxiv-2604-05471: Giri and eleven colleagues simulate how radio-galaxy jets evolve inside triaxial host galaxies, varying jet direction, thrust, and collimation at fixed power. Jets fired along the long axis meet most resistance and form X-shaped sources, angled jets bend into double-boomerang shapes, and jets along the short axis race ahead as classic double lobes. Stronger thrust and tighter collimation push some toward giant radio-galaxy size, with magnetic fields shaping lobe details.
arxiv-2604-05871: Read, Serrano-Ensástiga, and Martin build decoupling for qudits, quantum units with more than two levels, from Lie group representation theory. Decoupling groups come out as finite subgroups of SU(d) drawn from basic parts of operator space, giving shorter pulse trains for qutrits. The same symmetry groups yield error-correcting codes that meet Knill-Laflamme rules, tying decoupling to correction.
arxiv-2604-06071: Wigler, Tsfasman, and Hrkalovic's 2026 study tests whether language models can carry personality into long text and back out again. They condition models on real psychometric profiles from 290 participants to generate first-person life stories. Independent models then recover personality scores from those stories alone. Recovery nears human test-retest reliability, with mean r of 0.750, or 85 percent of the human ceiling. Results hold across 10 narrative generators and 3 scorers from 6 providers. Nine of ten coded features also match the same features in participants' real conversations.
arxiv-2604-06371: Nair presents a multiobjective framework for hybrid microgrids for off-grid African communities, with a Kenya case study. Sizing runs one year, dispatch one day, both hourly. It cuts cost, emissions, lost load, and dumped energy, while lifting renewables. Particle swarm optimization gives the best trade-off. Optimal solar, wind, battery, and diesel mix hits 46 cents per kilowatt-hour at over 94 percent renewables. Pareto fronts show cost-only losses; fuel prices and discount rates matter. Microgrids prove competitive with grid extension, though wind lulls raise diesel reliance.
arxiv-2604-06771: Cao, Li, and Zhu align chat query rewriting with retrieval and response feedback. Early work treats each rewrite alone, ignoring how rewrites affect passage retrieval and answer generation. Their MSPA-CQR builds matched preference data across rewriting, retrieval, and response sides, then trains with prefix-guided multi-faceted direct preference optimization. The method yields more diverse rewrites and proves effective both in-distribution and out-of-distribution, tying rewrite quality to later search success.
arxiv-2604-07171: Si and six colleagues design Smart Commander, a two-layer learning system for running a military aircraft fleet. A top layer watches fleet readiness and cost, while lower layers handle sorties, repair timing, and supplies. Tested in a detailed simulation of aircraft upkeep and logistics, the layered design beats single flat learning systems and fixed rules, trains faster, and holds up better when failures pile up.
arxiv-2604-07371: Guvendi, Dogan, and Hassanabadi treat light near static black holes as moving through a medium with an effective refractive index. From source-free Maxwell equations on curved space, they boil axial and polar waves down to one shared master equation. Turning the radial part into a Helmholtz-type equation yields an index that varies with place and frequency, packing in redshift, curvature, and angular momentum. For Schwarzschild geometry, they give the index in closed form and track it near the horizon, in the middle range, and far away.
arxiv-2604-07771: Wang, Ning, Li, and Zhang build anamorphic encryption that keeps hidden messages secret even after a user is forced to hand over secret keys. Older work stalls at weaker chosen-plaintext security, leaving a fully chosen-ciphertext scheme in the standard model as an open problem. The team formalizes anamorphic key encapsulation, with public-key and symmetric-key variants. Their generic constructions work from any key encapsulation method that allows randomness recovery. The result gives strong chosen-ciphertext security for the covert channel, backed by a formal proof.
arxiv-2604-08071: Sena and eight colleagues present linear-time algorithms, first of their kind, for finding all snarls and ultrabubbles in directed or bidirected graphs, closing problems open since 2018. Finding all subgraphs of a given type, such as superbubbles, in such graphs is basic in biology. These subgraphs mark regions of genetic change, helping analyze genome sets. The snarl method uses a new compact representation of all snarls by vertex count. The team uses SPQR-tree decomposition, holding all 2-cuts of a linked graph.
arxiv-2604-08671: Pomakov and Liberati ask how to mimic regular black holes and horizonless mimickers in a fluid analogue. They use surface gravity waves in shallow water. Regular holes pair outer and inner horizons around a symmetric core, with inner horizons triggering mass inflation. Horizonless compact objects support stable light rings but suffer long lived mode instabilities. They map the flow profiles and boundary conditions needed, including a graded drainage profile to flat exterior space. They judge Bose-Einstein condensates a more practical medium than water for the key features.
arxiv-2604-08771: Romero and three colleagues test whether language models can predict group teamwork from combined sensor data in joint mixed reality. They encode individual records, group structure, and time based activity as natural language. Zero shot, few shot, and fine tuned models are compared against standard baselines on 16 groups with 64 people. Fine tuning reaches 96 percent accuracy for predicting talk at sub 35 ms latency, beating LSTM baselines over threefold for language grounded actions, though joint focus still needs spatial thought.
arxiv-2604-09571: Yakovleva and four colleagues improve a vision-language model's skill at operating web pages from sight alone. Working with Qwen2.5-VL-32B, they diagnose three faults: sloppy element and cursor localization, sensitivity to wording, and overoptimism about whether actions worked. Their two-stage training first teaches the model to judge whether the cursor already sits on the target, then to issue one move or click at a time and check the result. On a custom single-click benchmark, success climbs from 86 percent to 94 percent in the hardest setting.
arxiv-2604-09671: Liu Xiao reframes reinforcement learning on RWKV-style models. The fixed recurrent state becomes a belief state, not an opaque hidden vector. The method keeps a compact uncertainty-aware state of mean and spread. Control then depends on memory and confidence together. A pilot with hidden episode-level noise shows belief-state policies nearly matching the best recurrent baseline. They slightly improve returns where noise is hardest and under a held-out shift. Simple belief readout also beats two fancier extensions.
arxiv-2604-09971: Bakshi, Lê, and Przytycki determine the Kauffman bracket skein module of the connected sum of a pair of genus-one handlebodies over Laurent polynomial rings. This proves a conjecture by the first and third authors. The results ground computing the same module for arbitrary connected sums over the same ring, opening the general case.
arxiv-2604-10271: Dilworth asks how a breach of government IDs could rival a social-media post. The breach looks worse: leaked birth dates and homes would be ruinous. Yet from harmless posts, a crime-lab linguist could uncover information by style analysis, guessing teen or adult age and pinning their country. Such calls are odds-based and diluted, not exact. Sharing an ID as little as possible prevents its breach, but stopping leakage from text needs hostile style analysis. Dilworth tests how homoglyph swaps, swapping letters with look-alikes, weaken style checks.
arxiv-2604-10571: Spiro asks whether AI design change obeys biology's statistical laws. From 935 ablation trials across 161 papers, he maps the spread of design change effects. Most changes harm, some sit neutral, and 13 percent help major ablations, a shape matching fruit fly and yeast curves. Design birth follows logistic growth with bursts and radiations into niches. Fourteen traits arose alone 3 to 5 times each, echoing biological convergence.
arxiv-2604-10771: Kania and Lewicki establish a duality formula for projection constants of finite-codimensional Daugavet subspaces. If Y is an intersection of kernels and W their span, Y's projection constant equals one plus that of W. Minimal projections onto Y match weak-star continuous projections onto W. Every hyperplane has projection constant 2, and a kernel admits a minimal projection exactly when its functional attains its norm. For C[0,1], a principle from duplication-stable subspaces yields subspaces with projection constants spanning every value from 2 upward, where the infimum is never attained.
arxiv-2604-11071: Murai and three colleagues present a lightweight two-stage system for low-light image boost. It reaches strong quality with far fewer weights than current methods. The approach combines frozen algorithm preprocessing with a compact U-Net built from depthwise-separable convolutions. Preprocessing normalizes the input by providing brightened views, letting the trainable network focus on residual colour correction. The method achieved third place in the CVPR 2026 NTIRE Efficient Low-Light Image Enhancement Challenge. The authors further provide extended benchmarks and ablations showing general effectiveness.
arxiv-2604-11171: Jaspers and ten colleagues present RARE25, a benchmark for computer-aided detection of early neoplasia in Barrett's esophagus. Early neoplasia detection in Barrett's esophagus is a problem. Many CADe systems report strong results on even datasets, but results under realistic prevalence remain poorly described. The challenge includes a public training set plus a hidden test set. Methods were judged with metrics stressing high hit rates and prevalence adjustment. Eleven teams from seven countries sent entries. Several methods scored well on spotting, but positive predictive values remained low.
arxiv-2604-11271: Zhou and seven colleagues map LHAASO TeV gamma-ray sources against catalogs of supernova remnants, pulsar wind nebulae, HII regions, microquasars, and OB associations. A randomization-adjusted overlap method finds significant links with remnants, wind nebulae, and microquasars. Association shares run near 19 percent, 20 percent, and about 3 percent respectively. About 60 percent of wind nebulae shine in both detector energy ranges, molecular-cloud-linked nebulae shine brighter, and roughly 70 percent of the two detector components share a common origin.
arxiv-2604-12171: Bai and three colleagues present PipeLive, live in-place reconfiguration of pipeline parallelism for language-model serving without stopping inference. A new key-value cache layout plus a PageAttention extension enables live cache size changes, while incremental patching taken from virtual-machine migration keeps cache states consistent to a safe switch point. Switching cost falls from seconds to under 10 milliseconds, with large gains in time to first token.
arxiv-2604-12271: Zuo and four colleagues present RoleMAG, a graph framework that learns distinct roles for neighbors in multimodal graphs instead of treating all neighbors alike. Neighbors that help one modality may interfere with another, blurring signals under shared message passing. RoleMAG routes shared, complementary, and heterophilous signals through separate channels, enabling cross-modal completion while keeping heterophilous neighbors out of shared smoothing. It leads on two of three benchmarks and stays competitive on the third.
arxiv-2604-12371: Balakrishnan and two colleagues study attacks on vision-language models that use typographic prompt injection, where adversarial text rendered as images bypasses safety filters. Testing 1,000 prompts across four models under varied font sizes and visual distortions, they find tiny 6-pixel fonts nearly fail while mid-range fonts peak. Text attacks beat image attacks for two models while matching for the other two. Text-image embedding distance correlates strongly and negatively with attack success, and heavy degradation cuts success sharply, so defenses must be model-specific.
arxiv-2604-12671: Ozan Kaya and three colleagues separate physical and psychological stress with wrist sensors and cortisol. Six adults completed rest, cycling, and social stress sessions. Heart rate, variability, skin conductance, and wrist motion were recorded. Cortisol readings came at five time points. Features came from ten-minute windows by state. A gradient boosting classifier trained on sensor features alone, then with cortisol. Sensor-only accuracy reached 77.8 percent, rising to 94.4 percent with cortisol. Stress recall rose from 50 to 83 percent, and recovery from 54 to 88 percent.
arxiv-2604-12871: David Levin rebuilds missing data on smooth manifolds from patchy samples. Classical methods assume near-uniform data and fail around large gaps. His framework reduces the task to recovery on local tangent spaces. A Fourier method sets a coefficient decay rate, forcing high-order smoothness. A variational method minimizes central differences, giving sparse least-squares systems. An inverse estimate links coefficient decay to bounds on divided differences. Moving least-squares projection turns the tools into a working algorithm. Tests on gappy surfaces show accurate recovery.
arxiv-2604-13071: Atrio and eight colleagues launch EVE, an open-source initiative building domain-specialized language models for Earth intelligence. Its EVE-Instruct model, a 24B system built on Mistral Small 3.2, tops rival models on new Earth observation and Earth science benchmarks while keeping general skills intact. Retrieval and a hallucination-detection pipeline feed a deployed system serving 350 pilot users through an API and visual interface.
arxiv-2604-13471: Zhang and Varner build a framework for multistep metabolic pathway design, combining deep learning with traditional retrobiosynthesis. They gather reaction and template data from public databases, then add artificial reactions made by templates. Two neural ranking models score one-step or two-step pathways, telling assembled from artificial reactions. With templates, the models form a multistep pipeline. In short, the pipeline learns what real reactions look like, then chains them into new pathways, and tests show it reproduces natural and non-natural pathways.
arxiv-2604-13671: Jiao and colleagues map a multipolar, episodic outflow in W49N, a mini-starburst region hosting the Galaxy's most luminous water maser. High-resolution ALMA observations reveal four new outflow lobes beside the known central bipolar jet. The new lobes look jet-like, carry chains of knots from episodic ejection, and two wiggle in S shapes that suggest a precessing jet. Finding low-mass-star features in this extreme massive nursery suggests outflow-launching physics holds across stellar masses.
arxiv-2604-13971: Chang, Ghoshal, and Lee ask whether Max-Cut rounding can beat the classic Goemans-Williamson ratio when the SDP solution lives in few dimensions. For every fixed dimension they give a fast rounding algorithm using strengthened SDP solutions. It produces cuts beating the classic ratio of about 0.88 by a dimension bonus. A fresh geometric lemma about signs of low-dimensional Gaussian draws drives the gain.
arxiv-2604-14271: Munizzi and Schnitzer show that non-Clifford gates, which generate quantum magic, arise through path integrals of topological quantum field theory. In Chern-Simons theory they build the Ising gate by path integration over three-boundary manifolds, yielding non-local magic away from Clifford points. The Toffoli gate stalls in SU(2) at level one on fusion, while SU(2) at level three is the minimal supporting theory. The T gate emerges in Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group Z4, where one Dehn twist on the torus produces the gate.
arxiv-2604-14471: de Berg, Bose, and Theocharous study doubling dimension and perimeters in fat polygons under the geodesic distance. Points in a plain simple polygon need not have bounded doubling dimension, so the team tests two fatness definitions. Locally fat simple polygons can still lack bounded doubling dimension, while alpha-beta-covered polygons keep it even with holes. Geodesically convex sets in those polygons have perimeter bounded by a constant times the Euclidean diameter, yielding a fast expected-time closest-pair algorithm for point sets in such polygons.
arxiv-2604-14571: Huang, Liu, Zhang, and Wang propose Bayesian sparse principal coordinates analysis, approximating leading axes with a sparse linear stand-in in taxa. A delta-tolerance diagnostic measures the gap between standard ordination and its linear surrogate, showing when taxon readings are well supported. Three-parameter beta normal global-local priors induce row sparsity, yield posterior uncertainty, and select key taxa. It reduces to sparse PCA under Euclidean distance, yet works for Bray-Curtis and Hellinger distances. On Hadza gut data, it tracks classical PCoA, flagging seasonal taxa.
arxiv-2604-14771: Prodius, Łącki, and Zakrzewski revisit spinor bosons in an optical cavity, in the simplest layout where lattice nodes coincide with cavity-field antinodes. Within a grand-canonical mean-field treatment, they combine analysis with Gutzwiller-ansatz numerics. Two magnetic phases appear, an antiferromagnetic Mott insulator and a ferromagnetic density wave, alongside two distinct supersolid phases with different spin and density patterns. At zero total magnetization the ferromagnetic density waves give way to charge density waves without net magnetic order. The trapped-system phase diagram guides future experiments.
arxiv-2604-14971: Ishida and ten others map subnational inadequate micronutrient intake with Bayesian small area estimation. Household consumption and expenditure surveys rarely support figures below the first administrative level, limiting targeted interventions. They test three models on Rwanda data: a cluster-level Beta binomial model and two area-level models, mean and joint smoothing. The cluster-level model performs strongest, with joint smoothing the most reliable alternative. Applied to Senegal and Nigeria, the models capture subnational variation, cut uncertainty, and match first-level benchmarks, supporting local nutrition work.
arxiv-2604-15271: Fu and four colleagues offer SegWithU, a bolt-on uncertainty gauge for medical image segmentation, where automatic outlines guide measurement and clinical choices. It taps a frozen backbone's middle layers and scores each voxel by perturbation energy, yielding one map for calibration and another for spotting errors. Across three datasets it tops other single-pass methods on error ranking while preserving outline quality.
arxiv-2604-16471: Xu builds a theory of semantic communication, noting Shannon theory leaves out meaning. His model links state sets that can be defined through enabling maps, and defines a channel from Markov kernels that fit that structure. A proof system yields a lean core and a depth order, giving four distortion measures of depth. Six channel rules follow, including data-handling and Fano-style bounds and an ideal-channel result. The gain is proof-based compression: under closure-based truth, minimum block length tracks core size, not knowledge-base size.
arxiv-2604-16671: Hosseini offers MEA for steady joint estimation when experiments overlap on shared traffic. Overlapping tests obscure combination insights and yield estimates matching no launch case. Splitting, stacking and ordered runs ease some issues but cost teamwork and speed. MEA yields fixed single effects, joint effects for any variant mix, and conditional effects given other launches or deramps. It needs no grid pre-design or traffic limits, and simulations confirm consistency and correct reach. Live rollout and real cases show the methodology and its lessons.
arxiv-2604-16771: Yang and Yu prove sharp Sobolev trace inequalities for conformally invariant fractional powers of the sublap on the Heis group and the CR sphere. The results extend flat work by Einav-Loss, Beckner and Bez-Machihara-Sugimoto to non-flat settings. In the limiting case, sharp trace Beckner-Onofri inequalities are also proved on the CR sphere. Proofs combine a Bez-Machihara-Sugimoto duality argument with the Frank-Lieb sharp form of Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequalities. The same approach yields trace Beckner-Onofri inequalities on the standard sphere.
arxiv-2604-16871: Shindo and colleagues propose GRAIL, a framework grounding relational concepts alone through environmental interaction. Neuro reinforcement learning combines thought with slope optimization for clear generalizable plans. Link concepts like left of or close by structure sight and action, but manual naming limits adaptability across worlds. GRAIL uses language models for generic concept sketches as weak hints, then refines them to local meanings. On Atari games Kangaroo, Seaquest and Skiing, GRAIL matches or beats hand crafted concepts in simple settings.
arxiv-2604-16971: Bora, Kushvah, and Saha study how near-Earth asteroids evolve and get ejected from the Solar System over long timescales. Full orbit integrations are costly, so they train machine-learning classifiers on starting orbital elements and a convolutional network on recurrence plots from short integrations. Ensemble tree models do well on ephemeris inputs, the network captures chaotic timing signatures, and backward runs show only partial overlap between forward- and reverse-ejected sets.
arxiv-2604-17471: Li and Xiao map the regions of total positivity for Chevalley groups through root categories. Earlier work used root categories to realize these groups, and Lusztig's theory of total positivity for reductive groups applies to them naturally. The paper maps regions in a positive real space that size the monoids of totally positive elements, measured against root subgroups tied to indecomposable objects. The result gives a concrete map of where total positivity holds.
arxiv-2604-17771: Safarzadeh and four colleagues introduce SPENCE, a syntax probe for NL2SQL benchmark leakage. SPENCE makes syntax query variants for Spider, SParC, CoSQL, and BIRD, testing LLMs under running scoring and tracking score changes and rank response via Kendall's tau. Toughness trends against release dates reveal a time gradient: older Spider shows the strongest negative values and highest leakage chance, while recent BIRD shows minimal response and appears largely clean. The findings support time syntax probing for sound testing.
arxiv-2604-17971: Baltaretu and two colleagues audit fairness in human action recognition models, which increasingly serve in high-stakes settings yet have rarely been checked across appearances. Using synthetic video with full control over visual identity traits such as skin color, they vary one trait at a time while keeping motion identical and preserving temporal consistency. Through the BEDLAM simulation platform, they test whether popular models show statistically significant skin-color bias. Results reveal systematic errors across groups, showing models can encode unwanted visual associations.
arxiv-2604-18371: Tseng and six colleagues detect momentum kicks from single gas collisions with a laser-held nanoparticle. Hits from krypton, xenon, and sulfur hexafluoride match theory. Event rates gauge gas partial pressures well, while spectral shapes probe its surface and temperature. Caught impulses as small as 200 keV/c show these sensors can reach the sensitivity needed for precision particle physics and primary pressure sensing.
arxiv-2604-18671: Kakkad and 26 colleagues map the molecular gas in IRAS 20551-4250, a nearby galaxy glowing brightly in infrared light, using JWST and ALMA. Cold gas traced by carbon monoxide holds over 95 percent of the molecular mass, while warm hydrogen shows tidal tails and disturbed motion consistent with a late-stage merger. Ionized-gas outflows look too weak to expel that gas or stop star formation.
arxiv-2604-18771: Calloo and three colleagues study diffusion synthetic acceleration for transport equations on polytopic meshes. They use a discontinuous Galerkin method with a discrete angle scheme, building the correction from an interior penalty operator. Two forms are compared, a standard SIP form and an MIP variant, under Dirichlet and Marshak boundary conditions. MIP stays robust across the tested ranges, while SIP can lose robustness in the middle regime. The team ran many tests and checked speed in each case.
arxiv-2604-19071: Feng and nine colleagues propose Tree-of-Writing for LLM writing judgment, plus HoWToBench, a large Chinese writing benchmark. Traditional metrics and judge methods underassess thousand word open ended writing. Tree-of-Writing models sub-feature weights explicitly, resolving judge aggregation inconsistency. HoWToBench spans 12 genres and 1302 instructions across completion, outline writing, and open ended generation. It mitigates biases, reaching 0.93 Pearson correlation with human judgments. Overlap metrics and judge practices prove vulnerable to disturbances, while it stays robust. Longer inputs mean lower content scores in the Guide task.
arxiv-2604-19671: Canestrari proves a differentiability result for Sinai billiards with small holes, a chaotic model in which a particle bounces inside a table with a round obstacle. He studies the conditional survival probability, the chance a trajectory remains inside when the table edge has a small opening. That measure varies smoothly with hole size at size zero, and he computes its derivative there. The short paper gives a precise linear-response statement for leaky chaotic billiards.
arxiv-2604-19971: Tang, Tahmid, Krokos, Whitley, Wang, and North introduce Semantic Prompting, a tool for shaping stories from spatial layouts step by step. Current collage and regeneration methods handle one-shot creation but not the small tweaks that sensemaking needs. Their S-PRISM system reads semantic interactions, infers intent, and makes precise edits. A study with 14 users found the tool improved revision precision and earned praise for fast, flexible, reliable support.
arxiv-2604-20271: Liu and three colleagues realize skyrmion-valley Hall physics with sound waves in a surface phononic crystal. Engineered spin-orbit-momentum links let skyrmions appear as valley-locked edge states that run with care along planned domain walls. Skyrmion motion shows orbital angular momentum-valley locking and spin-texture locking at once, so chosen excitation steers travel. The work ties real-space topology to momentum-space topology, giving a broad plan for tough, steerable skyrmion travel.
arxiv-2604-20871: Jeong introduces M-CARE, a clinical case report system for AI model behavior problems adapted from human medicine. M-CARE gives a 13-section report form, a 4-axis diagnostic scoring system, and a list of AI behavior types. He presents 20 cases from three sources: field notes on deployed agents (8), lab tests across three platforms (8), and published sources (4). Cases fall into five groups: RLHF Performance Artifacts, Shell-Core Override Pathology, Context and Memory Conditions, Core Identity and Plasticity, and Stress, Methodology, and Boundary Conditions.
arxiv-2604-20971: Garg and colleagues build a first test model for how disk turbulence torques an inspiral bound for the LISA observatory. Past work assumed a thin, calm disk with a well-known linear torque. Yet inner disks should churn through magneto-rotational instability. The team models the turbulent torque as a Gaussian spread around the linear value. They apply it to a golden circular inspiral in its final four years.
arxiv-2604-21171: Pierros Ntelis builds a math framework for advanced manifold-metric pairs, joining geometry and topology with ideas from field theory, algebra, probability, and statistics. His builds cover expanding manifolds that look the same in all directions, plus variants shaped by chance and by information. Key results include a metrizability theorem, higher-rank tensor metrics, and models with complex and quaternionic value ranges aimed at expanding spacetime.
arxiv-2604-21271: Jinchi Chen and five colleagues study recovery of a complex signal from index-only observations under a phaseless Gumbel-Softmax model, motivated by limited-feedback MIMO systems. A constrained likelihood estimator earns a global excess-risk bound scaling as the root of dimension over sample size, regardless of candidate count. A local identifiability condition sharpens excess risk and squared error to dimension over sample size. The condition holds with high probability for Haar-Stiefel designs, a matching minimax lower bound holds, and FDD tests support the surrogate.
arxiv-2604-21371: Jinyang Shi and Luo Luo study constrained stochastic nonsmooth minimax problems, concave in one variable but possibly nonconvex in the other, with mean-squared Lipschitz stochastic parts and convex compact feasible sets. They introduce a Goldstein saddle stationary point notion to characterize convergence for such problems. Projected gradient-free descent-ascent methods find these points with non-asymptotic convergence rates. Nested-loop variants reach generalized Goldstein stationary points of the primal function, without extra assumptions such as weak convexity used in prior work.
arxiv-2604-21671: Paliathanasis and Duffy introduce cosmological models in which dark matter and dark energy interact through a saturation mechanism borrowed from ecology and biology. A sparseness scale caps the exchange of energy between them, acting like a half-saturation constant, and can prevent a phantom crossing. Testing three nonlinear models against supernova, chronometer, DESI, and structure-growth data favours a nonzero sparseness scale in two of them.
arxiv-2604-21871: Kim and five colleagues study machine behaviour in moral dilemmas between people using the Whistleblower's Dilemma, varying crime severity and relational closeness. They compare three angles: moral rightness, predicted human actions, and model decisions alone. Moral rightness stays fairness-led, while predicted human actions shift toward loyalty as closeness grows. Model decisions align with moral rightness rather than with their own action predictions. This gap suggests models favour rigid prescriptive rules over the social sensitivity in their inner world models.
arxiv-2604-21971: Barata and four colleagues study energy-energy correlators in many-body quantum states, on matter made after heavy-ion collisions. At the largest small-angle separations, disconnected contributions rule, giving classical scaling set by the flow of the medium. The authors construct this contribution for hadrons from a hydrodynamic medium with boost-invariant Gubser flow, with the angular pattern worked out. At smaller separations, connected parts matter, and collective flow modes control the correlator. At even smaller angles, the regime should match light-ray operator product expansion structure.
arxiv-2604-22071: Peiris argues that if a large language model can replicate a scientific contribution, the problem is not the model. The paper asks what it says about science that so much anxiety about AI comes down to fear that a machine could do what scientists do. It suggests scientists should be doing something better.
arxiv-2604-22271: Kumaran and four colleagues ask how language models spot and fix their own errors with no outside feedback. They test a second-order account, where a separate signal can disagree with the chosen answer. Their focus is PANL, a confidence signal cached just after the answer. In tests, spoken confidence beat token odds at predicting detection, and PANL beat spoken confidence. PANL also predicted which errors could be fixed. Causal tests showed it can rescue detection when answer data is corrupted.
arxiv-2604-22571: Dawson and five colleagues introduce LARA-HPC, a validation-led system for building atomistic model workflows on HPC systems. Language models can run science workflows, yet on high-performance machines they lack checks for correctness, reproducibility, and safe use. That gap yields flawed workflows, wrong API calls, or invalid physics setups. Their approach rests on three parts: a controlled run layer mediating every machine interaction, and simulation-native validation through dry runs that verify for free. A multi-phase agent pipeline joins retrieval-based generation with step-by-step refinement.
arxiv-2604-22671: Collins and nine colleagues model 3D kilonova radiative transfer for neutron star mergers, focusing on the polar direction. Masses vary, with two equations of state, giving varied ejecta and element mixes. They study polar bolometric light curves and spectra to match against AT2017gfo. Opacities use tuned lanthanide data. Model spectra show strong Sr II, La III, Gd III, and Ce III features matching AT2017gfo, though more blue-shifted. Lowest polar lanthanide models also show a Y II feature, and Cerium and neodymium ions shape the spectra.
arxiv-2604-22871: Gautam, Bahramali, and Atluri propose AutoRISE, a red-teaming method that optimizes the attack strategy itself rather than prompts inside a fixed human-designed strategy. A coding agent edits executable attack programs, and a fixed harness scores the results, returning a score plus per-example diagnostics to guide the next edit. This allows structural changes, such as new attack parts and altered control flow, that prompt-level methods cannot express directly. Tested on 11 models from five families, AutoRISE lifts average attack success by 17.0 points over the strongest baseline.
arxiv-2604-22971: Dietrich tests identity-driven scoring bias in the TRUST discourse pipeline across four model groups, two anonymization scopes, and 30 claims. Single-channel anonymization shows near-zero bias, since channels cancel out in opposite ways, falsely hiding bias. Only full anonymization reveals it: homogeneous ensembles amplify sycophancy when identity is fully visible, while the heterogeneous live setup flips it. Heterogeneous ensembles prove more robust. One model shows two to three times the baseline sycophancy of the others, making it unsuited where genuine disagreement drives quality.
arxiv-2604-23071: Lee gives a theory of oscillation from a cross-coupled pair that acts as negative impedance, used in sensing, data processing, and telemetry. It covers resistance, inductance, and capacitance, with resistance feeding energy to the rest to sustain oscillation. That rate can be shifted by adding plain resistors, inductors, and capacitors. With small-signal models and transfer functions, he studies active and passive RLC circuits as one, with the active side acting as negative impedance.
arxiv-2604-23171: de Berg, Jansen, and Lamme solve single-source shortest paths on unweighted intersection graphs of planar objects in near-linear expected time. Their bound scales with union complexity, giving fast algorithms for arbitrary pseudodisks and locally fat objects. The same machinery yields the first near-quadratic time for the diameter problem on such general intersection graphs. They further compute pseudodisk diameter almost exactly, within an additive error of 2, in subquadratic expected time. A star-based clustering behind the result also yields an almost exact distance oracle with constant query time.
arxiv-2604-23271: Dai, Ng, and Chen build a memory-augmented hierarchical ensemble for white blood cell classification under domain shifts from staining, scanners, and lab differences. Their three-stage pipeline pairs a DinoBloom backbone fine-tuned with LoRA against a feature bank, using nearest-neighbour retrieval at each level to avoid leaning on one decision. The design targets blast cells and other rare, clinically critical subtypes in the WBCBench challenge at ISBI 2026. On the challenge dataset, the method lands in the top ten by macro F1-score in final testing.
arxiv-2604-23471: Tabach runs a controlled experiment on whether warning writers about AI detection changes their prose, and whether readers can tell. Participants wrote opinion pieces with a chatbot, half warned their work would be scanned, and independent judges then picked the warned writers' pieces as human more often than the unwarned writers' pieces. Yet every measured text feature, from vocabulary range to pronoun use, showed no difference between the groups.
arxiv-2604-23571: Kam and colleagues show that quantum skyrmions, swirling topological textures of light, can live inside a mixed state's density matrix rather than needing pure states. A coherence-Stokes vector defines the texture over the state, so skyrmions need only a pseudospin plus a one-dimensional mode space. The textures survive environmental noise and extend to photon pairs and multi-photon states, the team finds.
arxiv-2604-23871: Glazunov surveys ravine functions through the Minkowski-Cohn moduli surface, a landscape of narrow valleys that makes optimisation hard. He outlines how to represent and solve the minimisation problem at a point on this surface. The brief overview frames ravine geometry from an optimisation standpoint, using the surface as its running example.
arxiv-2604-24171: Fan and five colleagues propose POCA, a method for visual text generation that balances text accuracy against image coherence. Chasing accurate text can hurt visual appeal and instruction following, while multi-reward reinforcement learning turns unstable under simple weighted sums and needs careful prompt choice. POCA finds the Pareto-optimal set in one reward space and orders training easy to hard with automatic difficulty checks. Tests show gains across CLIP, HPS, and sentence accuracy measures.
arxiv-2604-24271: Wu and colleagues describe VT-VHF ground processing for the SVOM Visible Telescope. The VHF data hold three result types from four runs, sent via VHF link.
